eyebrow: Regex matching, built in as operators
caption: T-SQL's LIKE only has %/_ wildcards -- no inline regex like this.

code:
-- Matches 'Smith', 'smith', 'SMITH', 'sMiTh' -- all of them
SELECT * FROM customers WHERE customer_name ILIKE 'smith';
caption: No direct equivalent on SQL Server, Oracle, or MySQL.

eyebrow: DISTINCT ON: one row per group, PostgreSQL's way
code:
-- One row per customer: their MOST RECENT order only
SELECT DISTINCT ON (customer_id) customer_id, order_id, order_date
FROM orders
ORDER BY customer_id, order_date DESC;
caption: A well-known PostgreSQL-only idiom for 'latest row per group.'

eyebrow: The T-SQL equivalent needs a lot more code
code:
WITH ranked AS (
  SELECT customer_id, order_id, order_date,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id
                        ORDER BY order_date DESC) AS rn
  FROM orders
)
SELECT customer_id, order_id, order_date
FROM ranked WHERE rn = 1;
caption: Same result, window function plus a filtering CTE -- DISTINCT ON skips all of it.
